name: Shuffle cards smoothly
blurb: A clean riffle shuffle with a bridge finish is one of those small competences people notice immediately. It is a grip problem, not a strength problem.
gear: A deck of plastic-coated playing cards
steps: Split the deck roughly in half and hold each half in a mirrored grip: thumb on the near short edge, fingers on the far edge, middle finger providing pressure.
On a table, riffle the two halves together by releasing cards with your thumbs, keeping the inner corners close.
Push the interleaved halves together square, then arch them with your thumbs and release into the bridge.
Once the tabled version is smooth, learn the in-the-hands riffle, which needs the same grip with less support.
Learn a tidy overhand shuffle as an everyday alternative.
Practise squaring the deck after every shuffle — that is what makes it look expert.
tips: New plastic-coated cards shuffle beautifully; old paper cards fight you and teach bad habits.
Bend the cards less than you think. Big arches mean sprayed cards and bent corners.
proof: You riffle, bridge and square a deck in the hands, three times in a row, without a card escaping.
